newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rabin's grand-daughter says life a nightmare.
newsitem.headline: Rabin's grand-daughter says life a nightmare.

text.p: The grand-daughter of murdered Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin said on Wednesday her life had been a nightmare since he was assassinated by a right-wing Jewish militant almost a year ago.
In Tel Aviv, hundreds of Israeli youths marched with torches from the site where Rabin was shot by Yigal Amir to the hospital where he died.

Israel marks the assassination on Thursday, the anniversary according to the Jewish calendar. Television and radio stations broadcast special anniversary programmes on Wednesday night and family members were expected to hold a ceremony at Rabin's grave on Thursday.
"I don't remember much from those days...it's been one long nightmare since then," said Noa Ben-Artzi, whose eulogy moved world leaders to tears at Rabin's funeral.

"Everything that happened after the murder, if it was strange or ugly or painful, it doesn't resemble the things that happened before. My world is divided into two and if you ask me, it's clear that I would like to live in the old one," she told Israel Radio.
Amir shot Rabin at a Tel Aviv peace rally on November 4 to stop his government from handing over control of parts of the Israeli-occupied West Bank back to the Palestinians.

Rabin's 1993 handshake with PLO leader Yasser Arafat on the White House lawn signalled an historic conciliation with the Palestinians but transformed Rabin into a traitor in the eyes of some Jewish extremists.
"We are still wounded, we have an open wound...this wound won't heal so quickly," Rabin's wife Leah told Israel Television.
